lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: Back of the line, bless you. Everybody eats or nobody does.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: Pritchard sent you? He might have sent corn. Nine days in the bin, child, and ninety till the dogwood. And yonder sits my grain, tied to that painted hussy of a boat, with Lyle Hatcher selling it back by the cup.

buttons.label: Why not take it back yourselves?

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: The barge at my landing. And Lyle on that steeple by his neck, where the children can see what stealing bread comes to. I held him at his christening. I'll hold the rope. Mose has a skiff. Go on.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: He's two swivel guns on the rail and I've nine men who can stand up straight. I can count, child. It's the one thing I've left that works.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: That's a quarter cup short and I know it, so don't look at it like that. Eat. You'll want it. I'd tell you I've had mine, but the Lord's listening.

lines.speaker: pruitt
lines.text: River's up. River's always something.

lines.speaker: pruitt
lines.text: Granny send you? Then I'm to row you out. Front way's the gangway: buy a drink, look rich. Back way's her off side, where the barge is. Anchor chain's rotten at the third link. I, uh. I know that barge pretty well.

buttons.label: How do you know the barge?

lines.speaker: pruitt
lines.text: I towed it out. He said safe keeping. He gave me a dollar. I didn't know, I swear on the river I didn't. Don't tell her. I'll run the Chute for you at night, loaded, blind. Only don't tell her.

lines.speaker: hatcher
lines.text: Welcome aboard the Queen, friend. The first drink is on the house and the last one is on you.

lines.speaker: hatcher
lines.text: Sit, sit. Lyle Hatcher, Commodore by acclamation. You're Opal's new terrier. Now that barge was adrift, and I put a line on her, and that is salvage, friend, by a law older than this lake. Card?

buttons.label: Deal. The barge against my gun.
Who paid you to hold it?

lines.speaker: hatcher
lines.text: Well, I will be eternally... Ladies! Gentlemen! The house stands a round, for I have just been skinned by an artist. She's yours, friend, every sack. Now. Do you mean to give me to Opal? She means it this year.

lines.speaker: hatcher
lines.text: Ah. The lady turns, and she's mine. No, no, keep your iron, I've a drawer full. You have sand, friend, and I've a use for sand. There's a quarter of that barge in it if Greenwater hears she went down in the Chute.

lines.speaker: hatcher
lines.text: Two hundred, and a berth. Tell Opal the Chute took it. Delegate Belden has a soup wagon; he'll offer a bowl. I'm selling you a share, not a promise that his pot replaces the winter grain.

lines.speaker: hatcher
lines.text: Paid? ...You've been in my box. Or you're guessing, and I've told you. Ha! Yes. Silver, square mark: hold her till first frost, then turn her loose. But a man sees that much corn and that many hungry folk and thinks: Lyle, that's a market.

lines.speaker: pruitt
lines.text: One cut frees the barge for the Chute. Or burn the Queen. Thirty people are aboard - crew, cooks, the fiddler - and the winter grain is still lashed alongside. Fire can take them and the cargo. Say what you're ordering.

lines.speaker: pruitt
lines.text: WE'RE THROUGH! We're... oh Lord. Look how low she's riding. That's a third of it over the side. That's my doing. Tombstone Rock, I always cut it fine. Granny's going to count every sack.

lines.speaker: pruitt
lines.text: The cook was still aboard. The fiddler too; she taught me to waltz. We knew they were there. I can hear them in the water. Don't tell me this was only a boat.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: You won the barge from Hatcher? Every sack? Then we'll count it home. Now tell me what you mean to do with him. I want him on the steeple, and you know what that means.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: The grain is ours. Hatcher is dead. I can count both those facts without calling them the same kind of victory.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: Then eat somewhere else. I'll feed a thief's dog before I feed the hand that turned him loose. Bless you for the corn. Now get off my planks.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: We brought back less than we needed. Enough to stretch the pot, not enough to stop counting. We'll measure what came home before anybody calls it a victory. Thank you for what you brought.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: I asked for the grain and one man's answer. Now the cargo's burned and people are missing. Don't give me a number you haven't counted. Bring the living to the planks. We'll need every hand.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: The Chute. Yes. It had my husband and it had my daughter and now it's had the corn. You tried, child. Here. It's a short cup, but you earned it.

lines.speaker: starnes
lines.text: It's done. I thought I'd feel fed. ...Fifty years ago I put a spoon in that boy's mouth. Go on, child. There's corn. There's corn for everybody.

lines.speaker: belden
lines.text: Delegate Belden. The pot is for people who need it. We can discuss an agreement after supper, and you may refuse it. This wagon won't replace a winter's grain. It can keep people fed while they decide.

lines.speaker: belden
lines.text: Delegate Belden. The pot is for people who need it. We can discuss an agreement after supper, and you may refuse it. This wagon won't replace a winter's grain. It can keep people fed while they decide.
